parsed.explanation: Claim 3.2's proof begins 'Let T be a minimal (under inclusion) transversal of C' with no finiteness hypothesis, yet π is defined only on finite prime-sets, so 'Hence π(T) ∈ S_∞' is unjustified for infinite T. The witness is correct: {{x,t_n}: n≥1} is a pairwise-intersecting antichain of finite sets and {t_n: n≥1} is an infinite minimal transversal (removing t_n loses the edge {x,t_n}). Nowhere does the text prove minimal transversals of C are finite. The gap is load-bearing: in Step 4(c) the minimal transversal T ⊆ I∪Z_ω is necessarily infinite, since each g_s ∈ C is disjoint from I∪Z_s, which contains any given finite subset of I∪Z_ω, so no finite subset of I∪Z_ω is a transversal. Thus (iii) is invoked precisely on an infinite minimal transversal, which Claim 3.2 does not cover; nothing elsewhere repairs this.
